tour.overview:
On 6 June 1944, more than 150,000 Allied soldiers landed on five beaches of Normandy, code-named Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno and Sword, in the largest seaborne invasion in history. The beaches, cliffs and villages of the Calvados coast still carry the marks of that day and of the long battle that followed: bunkers, craters, memorials and cemeteries where tens of thousands of young men lie.

This private day takes you along the American and British sectors with a licensed guide who specialises in the battle. You stand on the cratered headland of Pointe du Hoc, walk on Omaha Beach, visit the Normandy American Cemetery, see the German battery of Longues-sur-Mer and the remains of the artificial harbour at Arromanches. In the morning or at the end of the day you can see the Bayeux Tapestry, which tells the story of another invasion, in the opposite direction, in 1066.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Bayeux or Caen, or Bayeux station (from Paris on request)
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; short walks on paths and sand

WHAT YOU SEE
• Pointe du Hoc.
• Omaha Beach and its memorials.
• The Normandy American Cemetery and its visitor centre.
• The Longues-sur-Mer battery.
• Arromanches and the Mulberry harbour.
• The Bayeux Tapestry (optional, morning or evening).

WHY THIS WORKS
Your guide adapts the route to your interests – American, British or Canadian sectors, airborne troops, or a relative who served – and avoids the coach parks at peak times.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, veterans' families, students and anyone who wants to understand D-Day where it happened.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you are coming from Paris for the day, ask us about the long version by car or by train to Bayeux; if you want to combine it with Mont-Saint-Michel, choose a two-day plan.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The American Cemetery holds a flag-lowering ceremony every afternoon. Sites are spread along 30 kilometres of coast; the car moves you between them. The weather on the coast changes quickly: bring a waterproof jacket.

days.name: Pointe du Hoc, Omaha Beach, the Normandy American Cemetery, Longues-sur-Mer, Arromanches and the Bayeux Tapestry
days.description:
What to expect: the landing beaches of 6 June 1944 with a specialist licensed guide, private car and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel or at Bayeux station at about 8:30. You drive west to Pointe du Hoc, a headland between Utah and Omaha beaches where the Germans had placed heavy guns that could fire on both. At dawn on D-Day, 225 US Rangers climbed the 30-metre cliffs with ropes and ladders under fire, only to find the guns had been moved inland; they found and destroyed them later that morning. The ground is still a moonscape of bomb craters and shattered bunkers that you can walk through.

You continue to Omaha Beach, the bloodiest of the five beaches, where the first waves of the 1st and 29th Infantry Divisions faced intact defences on the bluffs and suffered terrible losses before they broke through. You walk on the sand at Vierville or Saint-Laurent, see the Les Braves sculpture and the memorials, and your guide explains how the battle unfolded hour by hour. Above the beach lies the Normandy American Cemetery, where 9,388 American soldiers are buried under white marble crosses and Stars of David in perfect rows; the visitor centre tells their stories, and the Walls of the Missing list another 1,557 names.

After lunch in a village restaurant, you drive to the British sector. At Longues-sur-Mer, four German naval guns still stand in their concrete casemates, the only battery in Normandy with its original guns. At Arromanches, on Gold Beach, you see the remains of the Mulberry harbour, an artificial port towed across the Channel in pieces and assembled in a few days, which brought more than two million men ashore in the following months. Depending on your interests, the afternoon can include Juno Beach and the Canadian centre, the airborne sites of Sainte-Mère-Église, or Utah Beach. Back in Bayeux, you can visit the Bayeux Tapestry, 70 metres of 11th-century embroidery that tells the story of William the Conqueror's invasion of England in 1066. You are back at your hotel at about 17:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up in Bayeux or Caen.
09:15 – Pointe du Hoc.
10:30 – Omaha Beach.
11:30 – Normandy American Cemetery and visitor centre.
13:00 – Lunch.
14:15 – Longues-sur-Mer battery.
15:00 – Arromanches and the Mulberry harbour.
16:30 – Bayeux Tapestry (optional).
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Tell us if a relative served in Normandy: your guide can research the unit and visit the places it fought, and the cemetery staff can help find a grave.
• From Paris, the train to Bayeux takes about 2 hours 15 minutes; we meet you at the station.
• The Bayeux Tapestry museum is closed for renovation in some periods; we tell you when you book.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, lunch, bottled water, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: museum tickets (Bayeux Tapestry, Arromanches, Juno Beach Centre), drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we do this tour from Paris?
faq.answer: Yes. Either take the train to Bayeux (about 2 hours 15 minutes) and we meet you at the station, or we collect you in Paris by car for a long day of about 14 hours. We quote the version you prefer.

faq.question: Can you focus on the British or Canadian beaches?
faq.answer: Yes. Your guide can focus on Gold, Juno and Sword beaches, Pegasus Bridge and the British airborne landings, or include the Juno Beach Centre for Canadian visitors.

faq.question: Can you help us find a relative's grave or unit?
faq.answer: Yes. Send us the name, unit and any dates you have when you book. Your guide prepares the route, and the American Battle Monuments Commission staff at the cemetery can assist.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: The beaches, Pointe du Hoc, the American Cemetery and Longues-sur-Mer are free. Museum tickets such as the Bayeux Tapestry are optional extras.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch at a local restaurant. Vegetarian and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children interested in history; the bunkers and craters make the story very real. Some of the subject matter is serious, and your guide adapts the telling.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The cemetery and most sites have paved paths, and the car parks close to each one. Pointe du Hoc has uneven ground; the beach is sand.

faq.question: What is the flag ceremony at the cemetery?
faq.answer: Every afternoon, shortly before closing, the American flag is lowered with taps played. We can time the day to attend if you wish.

faq.question: Is it worth seeing the Bayeux Tapestry too?
faq.answer: Yes. It is a unique 11th-century work, and it gives a fascinating mirror to D-Day: an invasion from Normandy to England 878 years earlier.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes for paths and sand, and a waterproof jacket: the weather on the coast changes quickly.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October. Around 6 June the anniversary events are moving but very busy; book early. Winter is quiet and atmospheric but short and cold.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
